q: How long did 10 swings take in trial 1 with a 40 cm pendulum?
Calculate the mean time for one swing at 100 cm.
(20.1 + 19.9 + 20.0) / 3 = 20.0 s for 10 swings, so 2.0 s for one swing.
Describe the relationship between length and the time for one swing.
As the length increases, the time for one swing increases (0.9 s at 20 cm, 1.27 s at 40 cm, 2.0 s at 100 cm), but it does not double when the length doubles.
Explain why the student timed 10 swings and how the repeats show that the results are reliable.
Timing 10 swings and dividing by 10 makes the reaction-time error for each swing 10 times smaller. The three trials for each length are very close (within 0.3 s), so the results are reliable.
